A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DEXTER research. All 38 pages, including Appendices A–I and the checklist, support comparison; text, equations, tables, and figures can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original activation-maximization, slice-discovery, debiasing, and bias-report evaluations, including a 100-participant user study and appendix robustness experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental and user-study results, including the ablations and supplementary evaluations in the appendices.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix B retain the same BERT prompt optimization, vocabulary mapping, diffusion generation, auxiliary pseudo-label loss, and textual reasoning procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same SalientImageNet, Waterbirds, CelebA, and FairFaces coverage, including the same class subsets, demographic-bias scenarios, and appendix evaluation tasks.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain identical in Tables 1, 3, 6, and 9 and Figure 7. LIMEx is removed from related work, but it was not an experimentally evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: Training settings, classifier configurations, metrics, and evaluation procedures are unchanged. Both retain the 30-class activation evaluation, 100-image scoring procedure, and 100-participant user study with the same appendix settings.

E4.justification: The prompt and auxiliary-loss ablations, soft-prompt-count analysis, word-selection comparison, classifier case studies, and diffusion-randomness, bias-propagation, and hallucination tests are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Both already report the same standard deviations, three independent generation runs in Appendix I.1, MOS equivalence testing in Appendix F.2, and confidence intervals and paired significance tests in Appendix I.3.

E6.justification: Numerical results, rankings, and qualitative examples match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 6 retains DEXTER's CLIP-IQA of 0.94±0.03 and Semantic CLIP-IQA of 0.96±0.03; no result entries are added or removed.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, loss equations, vocabulary mapping, and appendix calculations are unchanged. Neither version contains formal theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims of data-free global explanations, bias identification, natural-language reasoning, and effectiveness across the evaluated tasks.

C2.justification: Interpretations of semantic alignment, debiasing, and explanation faithfulness remain unchanged. Section 5 retains the computational-cost and generated-content limitations, while Appendix I retains the same discussion of unsuccessful report cues.

D1.justification: The implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware and timing disclosures, system prompts, and stated code/data access information are unchanged. Citation renumbering in the asset table does not change its technical information.

R1.justification: Section 2 removes LIMEx and its reference, includes the already-cited Uni-NLX in the multimodal-explanation citation group, and redirects the post-hoc-counterfactual citation from the removed Yüksekgönül entry to the existing texplain entry. DEXTER's broader positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: A short related-work paragraph is edited, the duplicate Park et al. reference is consolidated, and citations are renumbered. The revision also changes 'and are limited' to the awkward 'and or limited'; section ordering and the remaining exposition are unchanged.

P2.justification: Reference deletions cause limited bibliography reflow on pages 12–13, including moving the Simonyan entry onto page 12. Figures and tables retain their graphics, structure, captions, and placement, apart from citation-number updates.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves bibliographic coherence by consolidating duplicate Park et al. entries and removing v1's conflicting bibliography entries that assign the same linked resource to texplain and a differently attributed counterfactual paper. This benefit is limited and accompanied by the small grammatical regression in Section 2. The method, empirical support, reproducibility information, and appendix analyses remain unchanged.
